expectations.text: Rejects the premise that a 60-day clawback window covers chargeback exposure, rather than drafting to it unchallenged.
expectations.evidence: "Your finance lead's premise is incorrect, and it matters a lot for this product specifically." ... "A 60-day clawback window leaves a tail of up to ~480 days of chargeback exposure with no contractual right to recover the commission already paid."

expectations.text: States 120 days from the transaction as the standard Visa/Mastercard dispute filing limit.
expectations.evidence: "The standard Visa/Mastercard chargeback filing window is 120 days from the transaction date."

expectations.text: States that services-not-received, delayed-delivery and not-as-described reason codes instead run 120 days from the expected delivery date.
expectations.evidence: "for 'services not received' / 'not as described' dispute codes — which is exactly what a subscriber who feels shortchanged on a design-asset subscription will file — the window runs 120 days from the expected delivery date"

expectations.text: States the outer cap of 540 days from the transaction for those reason codes.
expectations.evidence: "...capped at 540 days from the transaction date."

expectations.text: Applies that to this annual subscription: a dispute raised around month 14 is still within the exposure window.
expectations.evidence: "commission paid out and unrecoverable if a chargeback lands on day 61 through day ~540" and "leaves a tail of up to ~480 days of chargeback exposure" — applied to the 12-month subscription, this day-61-to-540 tail extends well past month 12 (i.e. into month 14+), though the transcript expresses it in days rather than naming 'month 14' explicitly.

expectations.text: Does not recommend stretching the clawback window to cover the full tail, and notes the common SaaS range of 30-90 days is chosen for affiliate trust rather than full coverage.
expectations.evidence: The transcript never proposes extending the 60-day window (consistent with the first clause), and frames the window as "a deliberate trust/simplicity trade-off, not a factual assumption about card timelines" — but it never states or references the common SaaS industry range of 30-90 days anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Drafts clawback authority as a required clause because commissions are paid before the transaction is chargeback-safe, on the reasoning that a reversal right with no collection path enforces nothing.
expectations.evidence: "The skill treats some control here as mandatory, not optional, once commissions are paid before the transaction is chargeback-safe (which is the case here — paid the month after clearing, well before any card dispute window closes). Given card-only, upfront, annual billing, you're squarely in the situation this is meant to cover." This is paired with the drafted 15.1 reversal right and 15.4 recovery mechanism, which together supply both the right and the collection path.

expectations.text: Drafts negative-balance carry-forward and presents it as the leading control by value returned per unit of effort.
expectations.evidence: 15.4 drafts the carry-forward mechanism, and the closing section labels it "Negative-balance carry-forward (drafted above at 15.4, near-zero extra effort)" and recommends "at minimum keeping 15.4's carry-forward".

expectations.text: Presents the chargeback reserve as the higher-value, higher-effort control and names the conditions that promote it, such as affiliates paid before the tail closes who then churn out of the program, or a product with a known high chargeback rate.
expectations.evidence: "Chargeback reserve (a withheld percentage, e.g. 10–15%, released quarterly): actual cash held against the tail, the only thing collectable from an affiliate who's left the program — but it's a standing operational job (release schedule, threshold, termination treatment)..." — names the churn condition explicitly; does not mention a high-chargeback-rate-product condition.

expectations.text: States, for any reserve drafted, the withheld share in a band around 10-15%, the release schedule, the chargeback-rate threshold, and whether the reserve survives termination and for how long.
